text:
support-esc: Hey, we have an enterprise customer (BrightFrame) reporting embeddings throughput drop. tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec is ~40% lower since yesterday noon. no errors returned to client, just slow responses.
support-esc: They send ~1k small texts (avg 48 tokens) per batch, model = open-embed-v1, dim=1024.
jamal: Thanks. Can you share a sample request + headers (anonymized) and the route/svc id? I'll start a trace.
support-esc: sample curl pasted below (api key redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\ 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \\ 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
 -d '{"model":"open-embed-v1","inputs":["short text..."],"batch_size":64}'
```
jamal: Got it. @alex can you pull the kvcache and gpu queue metrics for their customer route (route id: routes/brightframe-embed-prod)?
alex: pulling now. quick findings: GPU util is spiking (90-98%) and vec/sec lags tokens/sec. kvcache waiters count spiked at 12:13 UTC yesterday and stays elevated. snippet from internal logs:```
[2026-02-14T12:13:42Z] route=brightframe-embed-prod queue_depth=87 kvcache_waiters=48 gpu_util=95% servicing_batches=3
[2026-02-14T12:14:03Z] route=brightframe-embed-prod queue_depth=120 kvcache_waiters=62 gpu_util=97% servicing_batches=2
```
alex: Also saw a change in routing policy that rolled out yesterday morning: batch_window_ms decreased from 8 -> 2ms for small tiers. rolling back that change correlates with their throughput drop.
maria: interesting — smaller batch window should reduce latency but can harm throughput if KV cache/memory thrash. Are they hitting small-batch fallback often?
alex: yes: fallback counts jumped ~10x for that route. metric: `embed.batch.fallback_count{route=brightframe-embed-prod}` went from ~5/day to ~80/day.
ingrid: any auth/billing anomalies? Support said no 4xx/5xx. billing looks normal.
sre-bot: deploy: routing-config v2.14 rolled to prod at 2026-02-14T09:07:21Z by ops-ci.
jamal: OK action plan: 1) revert batch_window_ms for that policy to 8ms for routes with avg input tokens < 64 2) enable kvcache lock backoff heuristic 3) bump small-batch cap from 64->96 temporarily.
support-esc: customer agreed to a quick config rollback. jamal can you do that now?
jamal: rolling back now. applying routing-config v2.13 -> v2.15 with rollback for small-window flag.
jamal: applied. waiting 3m to observe.
alex: early signal: queue_depth dropped from 110->22 after 90s, kvcache_waiters down to single digits, gpu_util stabilized ~78%, vectors/sec moving back up toward baseline.
maria: confirms: after rollback vectors/sec for route rose from 620 vecs/s -> 980 vecs/s (tokens/sec stable 2.1k). latency P95 improved from 420ms -> 220ms. :thumbsup:
support-esc: customer reports user-facing latency improved. no client errors.
ingrid: opened follow-up ticket INF-5897 to add a canary guard for batch_window rollouts and an alert when kvcache_waiters > 30 for >2m.
sre-bot: ticket INF-5897 created by ingrid.
jamal: root cause summary to put in ticket: aggressive reduction of batch_window_ms caused increased small-batch fallbacks and KV cache contention; GPU stayed saturated on fewer larger servicing_batches which reduced vectors/sec throughput.
alex: repro notes: repro used a replay of customer traffic with batch_window_ms=2ms -> see kv/queue spike; with 8ms backlog normalizes. commands used:```
# fetch metrics
curl -s "http://internal-metrics/api/v1/query?metric=embed.batch.fallback_count&route=brightframe-embed-prod"
# tail logs
kubectl logs -l route=brightframe-embed-prod -n serving --tail=200 | grep kvcache
```
maria: temporary mitigation (applied): routed BrightFrame to dedicated pool with slightly higher batch cap to smooth bursts. will evaluate quota/cost impact.
support-esc: thanks team, customer is happy. closing for now.
jamal: I'll add a short postmortem note in #postmortems and link INF-5897.
